verdict.rationale: Weave's official tracing docs describe instrumenting functions with `@weave.op()` in Python and wrapping them with `weave.op()` in TypeScript, which shows first-party SDK instrumentation in both languages. The GitHub repo corroborates the Python `weave.op` tracing path. Only one documented snippet covers the TypeScript side. Missing for 10: TS/JS SDK package and installation details, documentation of feature parity between the Python and TypeScript SDKs, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the JS/TS SDK.

support.subject: As a developer, I can instrument apps in both Python and JS/TS with officially supported SDKs

citations.quote: When you decorate a function with `@weave.op()` (Python) or wrap it with `weave.op()` (TypeScript), Weave automatically captures its code, inputs, outputs, and execution metadata.
You can trace any function using `weave.op` - from api calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio etc
